reuse.why: Consumers share getExpectedAmount and reuse getApproxNumberThreshold, but the existing getScheduledAmount remains a parallel amount resolver.

duplication.why: The diff removes repeated consumer calculations, but duplicates missing/number/range dispatch between getExpectedAmount and getScheduledAmount.

placement.why: Schedule amount policy belongs in shared/schedules.ts, with API serialization and server consumers delegating to that layer.

scope.why: All edits concern schedule amount planning, its API representation, tests, or release notes.

maintainability.why: Centralizing most consumers helps, but overlapping amount helpers and contradictory furthest-from-zero documentation leave maintainers with competing definitions.

bypasses_abstraction.where: shared/schedules.ts: getExpectedAmount independently implements the amount dispatch already present in getScheduledAmount, while getScheduledAmount does not delegate to the new policy.

disguised_duplication.where: shared/schedules.ts: the missing/number/range resolver is reshaped into getExpectedAmount while the equivalent dispatch remains in getScheduledAmount; only range selection is shared.

abstraction_drift.where: getExpectedAmount introduces the op parameter and isapprox branch; getScheduledAmount remains an independent resolver bypassing it, so its existing consumers do not use the complete shared policy.
